taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts Dalea candida with recognized infraspecific structure. Texas native status is secure, but project target-zone county evidence remains unresolved.
look_here_first: Look for a perennial prairie clover with dense white cylindrical flower spikes and odd-pinnate leaves bearing several narrow leaflets; stems and foliage are conspicuously gland-dotted.

project_inclusion.range_basis: The prior review's explicit county was Williamson, which is outside the project's target-county list. Statewide Texas nativity and prairie distribution do not substitute for exact target-zone counties.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification; preserve the HOLD.

best_field_traits: conspicuous gland dots on stems and leaves
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Flower color is useful but not enough by itself; pair the white spike with leaflet number/shape and gland-dotted foliage.

confused_with: Dalea purpurea and related prairie clovers
comparisons.key_distinctions: Dense white spikes plus pinnate narrow leaflets and gland-dotted foliage are the strongest first-pass combination.
